cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest living among the exiles by the Kebar River (Ezekiel 1:1-3). The LORD has already had him draw Jerusalem on a brick and act out a siege against it (Ezekiel 4:1-3). Now God calls him 'son of man' and gives him a new sign to act out: shave his head and his beard, with a sharp sword.

cards.question: Ezekiel's about to shave his head and beard with a sharp sword. What does God tell him to use the sword as?

cards.text: A sword as a razor, on his head AND his beard. Friend, I get nervous when a cookie cutter wanders too close to my mustache, and this man's using a SWORD?
Once the hair is off, God tells him to divide it, and each third gets a job for when the days of the siege have ended.

cards.question: To divide his shaved hair into thirds, God tells Ezekiel to take a set of ___.

cards.text: I've weighed a LOT of dough in my day, friend, but never a haircut. The first third gets burned up inside the city.

cards.question: What does God tell Ezekiel to do with the second third of his hair, all around the city?
God tells Ezekiel to scatter the last third of his hair to the wind.

cards.text: Then God adds, 'For I will unleash a sword behind them.' He also tells Ezekiel to take a few strands of hair and secure them in the folds of his garment.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to take a few of the strands from his garment and throw them into the ___.

cards.text: A few tiny strands, one little flame. Then God says what comes from there.

cards.question: God says a fire will spread from where those few strands of hair burn. How far does He say it will spread?

answers.text: To the whole house of Israel

cards.text: Turns out the haircut was never about a haircut. The Lord GOD says, 'This is Jerusalem, which I have set in the center of the nations, with countries all around her.'

cards.question: God set Jerusalem in the center of the nations. How has she treated His ordinances compared to the nations around her?

answers.text: She rebelled more wickedly than they did
She kept them better than they did
She did about the same as they did

cards.text: And God doesn't leave it vague, friend. He says her people have rejected His ordinances and have not walked in His statutes.

cards.question: God says Jerusalem hasn't even lived up to the ordinances of the nations around her.

cards.text: So here it comes, and it's heavy. The Lord GOD says He Himself is against Jerusalem, and He will execute judgments among her.

cards.question: God's judgments on Jerusalem will happen out of sight where the nations can't see them.
Because of all Jerusalem's abominations, what does God say He will do to her?

answers.text: What He has never done before
What He did in Noah's day

cards.text: And He says He will never do it again. Fathers among her people will eat their sons, and sons will eat their fathers.
He says He'll scatter all her remnant to every wind. Then, as surely as He lives, the Lord GOD declares that they have defiled His sanctuary with all their detestable idols and abominations.

cards.question: Because Jerusalem's people defiled His sanctuary, God says He will still spare them.
Remember the three thirds of Ezekiel's hair? Now God talks about thirds of Jerusalem's people. How does the first third die within the city?

cards.text: The next third will fall by the sword outside the walls. And the last third God will scatter to every wind, with a sword unleashed behind them, just like the hair.

cards.question: God says when His anger is spent, He will be appeased. Once He has spent His wrath on Jerusalem's people, they will know that ___ has spoken in His zeal.

cards.text: And none of this happens in a back room. God says He will make Jerusalem a ruin and a disgrace among the nations around her, in the sight of all who pass by.

cards.question: When God executes judgments against Jerusalem, what will she be to the nations around her?

cards.text: And God keeps going, one picture after another. He will shower them with deadly arrows of famine and destruction, intensify the famine and cut off their supply of food.

cards.question: God says He will send famine and wild beasts against Jerusalem, and they will leave her people ___.

cards.text: Plague and bloodshed will sweep through, and He will bring a sword against them. Then He seals it: 'I, the LORD, have spoken.'
